description: A stage manager must remember special chair layouts, percussion changes, stand-sharing, and instrument swaps for different pieces in the same program so setup transitions do not rely on improvisation. All ensemble names are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 38-year-old stage manager coordinating a program with several quick setup shifts
user_profile.context: The performance order is fixed, but each piece changes the physical setup enough to create transition risk
user_profile.communication_style: Spatial and practical, wants setup states tied to the exact piece order

fact_sheet.fact: The Aethelgard Symphony Orchestra's concert is scheduled for October 26, 2024, at Crimson Hall.
The conductor for the performance is Maestro Elias Vance.
The first piece on the program is 'Overture to the Glass City' by Alistair Finch.
The setup for 'Overture to the Glass City' requires 66 musician chairs arranged in standard orchestral formation.
For the Overture, the percussion section needs one set of timpani, one 36-inch bass drum, and one crash cymbal stand.
The second piece is 'Symphony No. 3, The Mariner' by Elara Vex.
For 'Symphony No. 3', 12 additional chairs must be placed for the expanded brass section, bringing the total to 78.
An offstage brass choir of 6 players is required stage left for 'Symphony No. 3'; their music stands must be pre-set.
The third piece is the 'Concerto for Marimba and Strings' by Jian Li.
During the transition to the Marimba Concerto, all 44 wind, brass, and percussion chairs must be removed from the stage.
A 5.0-octave Marimba One 'Izzy' model must be rolled to position DS-C (Downstage Center) for the Concerto.
The marimba soloist for the Concerto is Kaito Tanaka.
The final piece of the concert is 'The Phoenix Ascendant' by Kaelen Rourke.
The transition to 'The Phoenix Ascendant' requires resetting the full 78-person orchestra chair layout within 5 minutes.
'The Phoenix Ascendant' requires two Lyon & Healy Style 23 harps, to be positioned behind the second violins.
The principal violist, Anya Sharma, switches from her standard viola to a viola d'amore for 'The Phoenix Ascendant'.
Anya Sharma's viola d'amore is stored in a locked case in instrument locker #117; the key is held by the stage manager, Lena Petrova.
For the entire program, the 2nd and 3rd clarinetists, Mark Olsen and Freya Holm, share music stand #22.
The principal cellist, David Rostova, requires a 16-inch-high, black wooden podium for his chair for all pieces.
The percussion setup for 'The Phoenix Ascendant' requires a glockenspiel, xylophone, vibraphone, and a large tam-tam in addition to the standard instruments.
The large tam-tam and its stand must be pre-set upstage center and moved into playing position during the final transition.
Stage manager Lena Petrova's master stage plot is a PDF file named 'ASO_Oct26_Plot_v4.pdf' on her company-issued tablet.
The stage crew chief for Crimson Hall is named Ben Carter, and he is the point of contact for any lighting or rigging adjustments.
The acoustic shell at Crimson Hall must be set to 'Configuration C' for the entire performance, which has a depth of 38 feet.
For 'Symphony No. 3' only, the 4th horn player has a separate, single-page part that must be placed on a wire stand to the left of their main stand.
The stage left crossover space has a clearance of exactly 48 inches, which is a tight fit for the marimba.
The maximum allotted time for the stage transition between 'Symphony No. 3' and the 'Marimba Concerto' is 4 minutes.
The 2nd oboist, Clara Bellini, doubles on English horn for 'The Phoenix Ascendant' and requires a K&M dual peg stand at her seat.
All musician chairs are black Wenger Nota Standard models, except for the 6 double bassists who use adjustable Wenger Nota stools.
The two percussionists covering the mallet instruments for 'The Phoenix Ascendant', Sam Jones and Maria Flores, require four padded music stands for their parts.
